3. The defendants appeared in the suit by filing written statement. Thereafter, the defendant No.I filed an application for temporary injunction stating that the lands described in schedule 1 to 6 belonged to Amjat Ali; that Amjat Ali died leaving behind two daughters, the plaintiff and the defendant No.1, 1 widow the defendant No.2 and defendant Nos. 3-43 as residuaries; that during pendency of the suit by amendment of the plaint, the plaintiff added schedule No. 7 and claimed share alleging that the lands of schedule No, 7 also belonged to Amjat Ali which he purchased in the benami of defendant No.1; that the defendant No.1 is contesting the suit by filing written statement and claiming that when the defendant No. 1 was a child, Amjat Ali purchased the said land in her name; and that the land of schedule No.7 of Title Suit No. 52 of2009 belonged to the defendant No. I along with the predecessor of defendant Nos. 29-33 namely Helal Uddin and Tobarok Hossain and they got the same in equal shares by registered sale deed dated 28-4-1955 and the defendant No. 1 by an amicable settlement with the other original owners got 0.0733 acres of land at the southern side of the plot being clearly specified and demarcated by boundary marks and defendant ,No. 1 constructed semi-pucca shop houses thereon and she also paid the rents of the same to the Government and the SA Khatian No. 867 in respect of the above land has also been recorded in the name of this defendant No. 1 and the defendant Nos. 29-33 did not hold any right, title and possession over the same; that the defendant No. 1 resides in Dhaka with her sons and daughters; that the defendant Nos. 29~33 are holders of hind contiguous to the scheduled land; that due to absence of the defendant No. 1, the defendant Nos. 29-33 have become greedy to grab the schedule land by encroachments and are also threatening that they will construct multi storied building on their land covering the portion of the defendant No.1; that on 17-4-2009 the defendant No. 29 disclosed to the son of the defendant No.1 that they would construct multi storied building thereon by dispossessing the defendant No. 1 and for that the defendant No. 1 was compelled to file the application for temporary injunction against the defendants Nos. 29-33.; that the balance of convenience and inconvenience lies in favour of the defendant No. 1; that the defendant No. 1 has prima facie case in respect of the suit land and in case of refusal of temporary injunction she will suffer irreparable loss. 

 15. It is also stated in the ground that the learned District Judge committed illegality in holding that the defendant No.1 has succeeded in making out a prima facie case' in respect of the 1/3rd share in 0.07 acre from southern side of plot No. 2063 and during SA operation her share was recorded in SA Khatian No. 867. in her name and she constructed pucca structures at her expenses and that she did not admit plea of dispossession . by the contesting defendants in her petition for temporary injunction instead of holding that she lost her right, title and interest in respect of the suit land by judgment and decree of other suit No. 31 of 1964 and she admitted the plea of dispossession by her application for mandatory injunction dated 16-9-2009 and, as such, the impugned judgment and order is illegal and liable to be set-aside. 

 27. The appellate court discussed that the contesting defendants case is that the 0.22 acre of land of CS Plot No. 2063 of Mouja Karimganj recorded in CS Khatian No. 882, which is a part of the land of schedule No. 7 along with other lands were purchased by the defendant No.1 jointly with Helal Uddin and Tobarak Hossain but they have got the portion of land belonging to the petitioner (defendant No.1) by amicable partition. She was given another land in exchange of the disputed land but the defendant did not mention in exchange of the disputed land and number of plot. The defendant No. 1 asked the defendants to state the plot number and khatian number of the land given to the defendant No.1 but they mentioned a plot number without any document. So, it is not proved that the defendant No.1 got the land in exchange of the suit land. It also appears that the defendant No.1 -appellant got 0.0733 acre of land out of the suit plot No. 2063 from the southern side of the plot specified and demarcated by boundary marks and it was recorded in the name of the defendant No. 1 in SA Khatian No. 867 which is adjacent to Karimgonj Bazar and her share was also marked as holding No. 88 by the local municipality. She has been regularly paying rent to the Government and taxes in respect of the disputed land. She constructed pucca structures at her expenses but the defendant Nos. 29-33/42 having no prima facie case and possession have been threatening the defendant No. 1 with dispossession from the suit land. 

 31. The appellate court after proper and elaborate discussions of the facts and circumstances of the case and on considering the decisions reported in so many cases found that the defendant No.1 has able to prove that she has prima facie title and exclusive possession in the suit plot wherein she has been in possession of 0.0733 acre of land from the southern side of the plot No. 2063 specified and demarcated by boundary marks and it was recorded in the name of the defendant No.1 in SA Khatian No.867 which is adjacent to Karimganj Bazar where she constructed pucca structures at her own expenses.
